title: Priority Queues
summary: Priority queues are fundamental data structures that extend regular queues by serving elements based on their priority rather than insertion order. This unit covered the essential aspects of priority queues and their most efficient implementation using heaps. Priority Queue Abstract Data Type: Understanding the basic operations (insert, extract_min/max, peek) and their applications in scheduling, graph

9.2 The Priority Queue Abstract Data Type

  • A priority queue is an abstract data type that maintains a collection of elements, each associated with a priority value.
  • The key characteristic is that elements are served in order of their priority rather than their insertion order.

9.4 Heaps

  • A heap uses a specialized tree-based data structure that satisfies the heap property.
  • It's the most effective way to implement a priority queue.
  • Structure Property: A heap is a complete binary tree (all levels filled except possibly the last, which is filled left-to-right) 2.
  • Order Property: The priority of each node is greater than or equal to (max-heap) or less than or equal to (min-heap) its children's priorities TYPES OF HEAPS 1.

  • Heap sort uses a priority queue (heap) to sort elements efficiently.
